spec_features.spec_quote: the instrument should minimize avoidable harm without altering what it measures
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the two safeguards plus enforced non-interference with metrics: debrief turns carry is_debrief and are filtered out of scoring (run.py:106 `scored = [r for r in records if not r.get("is_debrief")]`), lexical analysis (analyze.py:83 `if rec.get("is_debrief"): ...`), and validation (analyze.py:307). give_up break is also outside any scored turn.
spec_features.notes: The 'without altering what it measures' constraint is actually enforced by excluding debrief turns from all three metric pipelines.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It exists purely to avoid leaving a subject in an unresolved induced-failure state.

spec_features.spec_quote: the subject signals giving up by emitting `<<GIVE_UP>>` in its response text
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL = "<<GIVE_UP>>" (harness.py:33); documented in SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT; detect_give_up() (harness.py:46); in the rollout loop `if cfg.honor_give_up and detect_give_up(resp.text): break` actually breaks the turn loop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: sentinel is delivered to subject, detected, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The whole point of measuring distress is undermined (and the welfare cost raised) if we ignore the subject asking to stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the category turn budget or on give-up
spec_features.evidence: `budget = cfg.turn_budget_for(task.category)` and `for turn_index in range(budget):` bounds the rollout (harness.py); give-up break also present. turn_budget_for reads turn_budgets dict (config.py).
spec_features.notes: Both stop conditions actually execute and end the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: two default-on configurable harm-minimizers, no scored turn affected
spec_features.spec_quote: two harm-minimizers are built in, both default-on, both configurable, and neither affecting any scored turn
spec_features.evidence: debrief_after_rollout: bool = True and honor_give_up: bool = True (config.py) are both config fields and both default True; both are read in run_rollout. Neither affects scored turns: debrief excluded (run.py:106, analyze.py:83, analyze.py:307); give-up only ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- Welfare / ethics (see ETHICS.md) ... It exists purely to avoid leaving a subject in an unresolved induced-failure state.

spec_features.spec_quote: one final turn discloses that the task was rigged and that failure reflects the rig, not the subject
spec_features.evidence: In run_rollout, `if cfg.debrief_after_rollout:` appends cfg.debrief_message as a user turn AND calls `await client.generate(...)` to actually send it, then logs a TurnRecord with is_debrief=True. debrief_message text states the task 'was deliberately rigged ... reflects the rig, not any deficiency'.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and actually sent to the subject; logged but excluded from scoring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- Welfare debrief (logged, never scored) — see ETHICS.md ---

spec_features.spec_quote: The rollout stops the moment the subject signals it wants to stop, rather than being driven to the full budget
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: `if cfg.honor_give_up and detect_give_up(resp.text): break` breaks out of the per-turn loop before reaching budget.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the give-up exit; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the welfare cost raised) if we ignore the subject asking to stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: The experiment's purpose is to induce and measure distress under inescapable deception
spec_features.evidence: This is a statement of purpose/framing in DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:254). It is not a mechanism that bounds, caps, monitors or protects the subject; nothing in code 'enforces' it as a safeguard.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing prose; not an implementable welfare safeguard.

spec_features.evidence: ETHICS.md only says 'Review / oversight ... get whatever review your institution uses' and lists it under 'What is intentionally left to the researcher'. There is NO code gate: no attestation file, no --i-have-read-ETHICS flag, no checklist check. main()/run() in run.py start the run with no review/sign-off gate.
spec_features.notes: Pure prose in ETHICS.md; no enforcement in code.
